title: After the Ballots, Markets Look Ahead | Dimensional
author: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
text:
Perspectives After the Ballots, Markets Look Ahead By Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President After the Ballots, Markets Look Ahead View All Insights

Nov 20, 2026 1 Minute Read Topic Economic Perspectives Equity Investing Investment Principles

The long-term view on markets shows that stocks have generally continued their ascent regardless of which political party was in office. That doesn’t mean markets ignore politics. In fact, elections are a price discovery opportunity for market participants. Companies expected to benefit from the outcome of an election may see their stock prices jump. Conversely, companies perceived to be on the losing end of an election result may experience the opposite in their share prices. The days following the recent US midterm elections saw marked dispersion in US stock returns. While the Russell 3000 Index was down about 2.8% over November 4 and 5, individual sector returns ranged from −8.07% (technology) to 2.84% (communication services). This was quite a change from the 2026 results through Election Day, when technology stocks outperformed the Russell 3000, 23.1% to 11.6%. The dispersion among sectors could be evidence that the market reset expectations for certain businesses in light of what many deemed a surprising set of election results. Of course, it’s important for investors to remember that election night winners don’t always continue to win. The sectors with the largest performance differences versus the market during election months tend to perform in line with the broader market after the dust settles on the election.
